They will likely prevail. Trespassers are generally owed only a duty to avoid willful or wanton injury, but a company that knew its discharges were fouling a lake that squatters were drinking from and bathing in could readily be found to have acted wantonly, and many jurisdictions have abandoned the trespasser distinction in favor of general reasonable-care rules. The estates' main hurdles are proving the company knew the squatters were using the lake and proving that the contaminated water caused each death.
